Exact rational checks covered 304 beta identities for d=3,...,18 and balanced Schur coefficients for even d=4,...,18. Within-block symmetry keeps these spectra stationary under the invariant perturbation.

G-S3 | Lemmas 4.1-4.2 and Theorem 4.3, pp. 5-6,11-12: the strict cross-gap supplies a unique maximizing plane even with internal eigenvalue collisions. Fixed cutoffs, exponentially small exterior/annular contributions and Gaussian polynomial domination support C2 control. On the labeled trace-zero sphere, Hess(h_r)=-h_r/R^2 times the metric; this makes the large-s optimizer exactly two-block, beyond mere asymptotic convergence.

The first-exit coexistence-or-degeneracy alternative follows from compact separation and local strictness. The physical-radius bound satisfies both eigenvalue constraints. No claim of a first-order or unique transition is needed.

The inward boundary derivative and large-lambda radial concavity produce an interior maximizer. Haar covariance gives the correct source marginal, and equation (25) yields the posterior-mean report. Thus the stronger, corrected equality condition in G1 is met here.

The coefficient r(d-r), distortion rescaling r^2/(d-r)^2, and Born-query factor 1/[d(d+1)] are consistent.

Counterexample: d=2,r=1,lambda=10 and constant A=0. The stated Gibbs posterior is Haar and Q is constant, yet I+lambda D=5. A source-orbit report has Q=(1-exp(-20))/20, so the right side of (5) is at most 2.9957322756, strictly below 5. Theorem 6.1 is not invalidated because Theorem 5.2 separately establishes that its reports maximize Q.

Equation (37) needs pi^[r(d-r)] multiplying the same c_d,r. For d=2,r=1, c_2,1=1/pi and A=diag(a,b), the exact normalizer is (exp(sa)-exp(sb))/(s(a-b)); (37) is smaller by pi at leading order. This shifts the unspecified constant in (13), not spectral derivatives. Proposition 5.1 independently supplies the correct RDF normalization, so the main high-rate constant survives.

The explicit outer factor and 2x2 inner completion establish attainment, while the inverse problem is reduced to a single cubic with a monotonicity/Sturm-compatible uniqueness argument. I tested boundary and asymmetric fixtures through the supplied exact programs and found no counterexample. The result relies on classical degree-one Blaschke-Potapov and degree-preserving completion theory; the cited primary source supports that general structure, while the manuscript's special scalar construction makes most of the needed converse explicit.

assessments.summary: This exact fourteen-page v1 manuscript makes a substantial and largely convincing connection between finite-dimensional matrix-Bingham spectral optimization and unrestricted high-fidelity rate-distortion on complex Grassmannians. The cubic Haar moment selects a positive one-spike weak-field orbit for 1<r<d/2, whereas a uniform differentiated Laplace expansion selects the rank-r two-block orbit exactly at sufficiently strong field; the mismatch forces nonanalyticity of the optimized envelope without overclaiming a first-order or unique transition. The information-theoretic half correctly reduces arbitrary standard-Borel memories to the posterior-density body, localizes the Shannon dual near its extreme orbit, and constructs a covariant Bingham channel whose posterior mean is the optimizing report. The Jacobi-Selberg calculation yields the stated sharp high-rate constant and complement transfer. I found no material contradiction. The existential thresholds and global analytic localization are not computationally reproduced, and the appendix's uniformity/quotient-Hessian steps deserve careful expert attention, but I did not identify a counterexample or a missing condition that invalidates a main result.

Appendix A addresses the key need for two differentiated orders, including uniform exterior tails, Gaussian rescaling, and internal block collisions.

assessments.summary: This exact 14-page v1 supports its principal Hilbert-rank, singular-branch, Segre and harmonic-spectrum conclusions. The annihilator proof and Bell exposure are sound, and the three-sector tightness obstruction survives exact checks. The contribution is a useful synthesis of classical geometry and discrimination bounds, rather than a new polynomial method or tester theory. A substantive presentation issue is that canonical tester compression already extends the Hilbert probability bound to arbitrary families, so orbit transitivity is not needed for the advertised upgrade. I found no unresolved objection invalidating the stated main theorems; minor revision is appropriate for this scope/novelty distinction and replay documentation. The score reflects strong incremental research, with incomplete priority verification and no claim of operational saturation.
strengths: Theorem 3.1, p.4: the annihilator of span{U^tensor k} is exactly I(X)_k; quotient dimension therefore gives H_X(k). Vectorized parallel Bell outputs expose that entire span, so the maximum causal-support assertion is an equality, not merely an upper bound.

Theorems 5.1 and 6.1, pp.6-8: the quadric, traceless projective plane and central point give distinct correct branches. For selective-phase qudits L_c(X)=Tr(X)I+cX has eigenvalues c+d and c; the physical exceptional singularity c=-d occurs only at d=2,c=-2. The Segre Hilbert count and two-query defect follow.

Theorem 8.1 and Proposition 8.2, pp.9-10: the zonal kernel (a+b n.m)^k gives the stated Legendre moments and multiplicities. Integrating its square yields the purity formula and linear participation dimension for a fixed interior angle; endpoint parity and rank losses are consistent.

Theorem 9.1, p.11: equal top harmonic eigenvalues force a/b=1/(2k+1), after which the third-sector ratio is k(2k+3)/(2k+1)>1. Sector-trace invariance also justifies the positive-reweighting obstruction; this is stronger than checking only uniform designs.

Theorem 7.1, p.9, correctly separates rank from attainable success through positive scalability KCK=K. The manuscript also correctly warns that antipodal traceless axes are identical channels and that necessary query bounds do not construct attaining protocols.
weaknesses: Sections 4 and 12, pp.5,13: the causal-versus-GEN boundary is unnecessarily restrictive. Put v_i=|U_i>>^tensor k and w_i=W^(1/2)v_i. Equation (5) makes w_i unit vectors; W^(-1/2)T_iW^(-1/2) is a POVM on supp W. Their span has dimension at most H_X(k), giving the same H_X(k)/M bound for arbitrary families. This weakens the claimed special role of orbit leverage but does not falsify Theorem 4.2.

Novelty boundary, pp.2-3,13-14: Bavaresco-Murao-Quintino Theorem 5 and Appendix F already contain the ambient cap and group-average domination (https://arxiv.org/html/2105.13369v3). The credible additional content is the exact promise geometry and spectra. The special 24-echo predecessor [11] was not retrieved, so its overlap and priority remain unverified.

Section 12 calls the verifier range configurable, but the supplied main() hard-codes its ranges and has no command-line range option. Its leverage check sums harmonic multiplicities rather than constructing an orbit average or a tester. This is narrower evidence than a direct operational verification.

The supplied reproducibility README refers to verification/ and paper/ layouts and manuscript sources absent from this batch. The exact checker runs directly, but the release rebuild and package_release.py --check were not reproduced. No failure of the supplied canonical PDF hash is implied.

Sections 11-12: exact rank is discontinuous at singular promises and does not quantify noisy discrimination or the attainable success of generic finite subsets. The manuscript acknowledges these limits; they cap the practical significance of the asymptotic support exponent.
potential_errors: Lemma 4.1, p.5: transitivity of an abstract action on a set of unitaries alone does not imply a unitary representation on their Choi-vector span. State the linear/unitary covariance assumption used in the proof. The conjugation actions in all concrete applications satisfy it, so this is a formulation issue rather than a demonstrated application failure.

Section 11, p.13: the necessary query scale is said to drop when the support exponent decreases. For fixed d and large M, M^(1/(2d-2)) grows faster than the ambient M^(1/(d^2-1)); the promise strengthens (raises) the necessary query count. The displayed formula is correct.

The combined Theorems 8.1, 9.1 and 10.1: exact sphere/circle spectra, endpoint cascades and the all-k Bell-tightness obstruction form a potentially useful package for constrained oracle discrimination. Priority is a candidate assessment, not an exhaustive literature conclusion.

assessments.summary: The exact 11-page v1 gives a convincing local stability theorem, with a necessary criticality hypothesis that the half-Grassmann applications actually satisfy. Its Jacobi Hessian reduction and weak-field threshold survive symbolic replay and independent exact checks, including the sixth-moment boundary. The near-balanced metastable branches correctly invalidate an indiscriminate saddle shortcut, while the balanced branch remains locally stable at every positive field. I found no unresolved objection capable of invalidating these main claims. Minor revision should clarify the zero constant coefficient in Section 8, the field-order convention for the Hessian signs, and reproducibility details. Global spectral optimality, all-distortion rate-distortion and exhaustive novelty are not established and receive no credit as proved results.
strengths: Lemma 2.1 and Proposition 2.2, p.3: averaging the addition theorem over both source-orbit variables produces squared harmonic means. A proper compact orbit cannot carry ambient uniform measure, so a nonconstant mode is present; positive exponential coefficients make the spherical Laplacian strictly negative for every t>0.

Lemma 3.1 and Theorem 3.2, pp.3-4: the gradient lies in the normal isotropy fixed space. At a critical orbit differentiating invariance annihilates tangent and mixed Hessian terms; self-adjoint equivariance and the stated block symmetry then turn the negative trace into strict normal definiteness. The torus example correctly shows why orbit constancy alone is insufficient.

Theorem 4.1, pp.4-5: the real dimensions, two traceless diagonal normal modules and off-diagonal tangent directions are consistent. Block-swap composed with sign reversal fixes the balanced point and exchanges modules, while the stabilizer has no fixed traceless vector. This supplies the missing hypotheses over R,C,H for r>=2.

Lemma 5.2 and Theorem 6.1, pp.6-7: direct symbolic differentiation of the stated Jacobi generator at k=1..4 confirmed LY=-2rY and LS=k(2r-k)/2+2Y^2-4rS. The posterior covariance and spherical multiplier combine with the displayed denominators to give the two scalar Hessian operators; k=1 is correctly excluded from positive-block splitting.

Theorem 7.1 and Appendix A, pp.7-10: exact replay confirms both quadratic coefficients and the sixth-moment boundary. Independent integration of x(1-x)y(1-y)(x-y)^2 at r=3,k=2 gives mu2=2/35, mu4=1/105, mu6=4/1617, [u^2]Hminus=0 and [u^4]Hminus=-1/16170. The boundary instability therefore survives a check independent of the Schur expansion.

Proposition 8.1 and Section 9, pp.8-9: the pointwise S<=k/4-Y^2/k inequality yields the moment-ratio tail bound. The paper does not promote the finite remaining gate into an all-rank theorem and does not infer global optimality from the absence of a balanced spinodal.
weaknesses: Theorem 3.2 is structurally persuasive but the applications compress several representation-theory facts into one paragraph. Explicit stabilizer groups and normal-module dimensions, especially for quaternionic r=2, would make the real irreducibility and zero-fixed-vector checks easier to audit without changing the proof mechanism.

Section 8 proves eventual negativity of coefficients, not negativity of Hminus at every field for every multiplicity. For 2r/3<k<r the positive low-degree term is real, consistent with metastability. Any later global sign or phase claim still requires the stated low-degree/value-comparison work.

Section 10: the Bessel replay checks positivity of isolated formula terms on 60 cases; it does not compute orbital coefficients q_l or a full Grassmann Hessian. The ambient-dimension dictionary restates expressions rather than independently counting modules. These are limited diagnostics despite a successful run.

The replay depends on SymPy and mpmath, while the supplied README says only Python 3 and contains no pinned dependency file. The first execution stopped at missing mpmath; installing local dependencies resolved it. The supplied Lean README explicitly contains no formalization.

Selected source inspection confirms the Jacobi-density antecedent in Dumitriu-Edelman, Eq. (5), and the trace-transform framework in Forrester-Kumar (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2011.00787). Low-degree moment gaps are explicit; the finite-certification tail bound is valid; the Gr_C(3,6) inequalities use a credible coefficient induction; the Gr_C(4,8) exact block overlaps the analytic tail; and four density sign changes plus total positivity give the unique Gr_C(2,5) canonical crossing. strengths: Theorem 3.1 exposes the multiplicity defect r^2-q=(r-k)^2 and reduces degrees four through ten to rational expressions with positive-coefficient certificates, including separately listed low-rank exceptions.

Theorem 4.3 gives a real finite certificate rather than an asymptotic slogan: a translated and scaled event in the uniform Hermitian matrix interval supplies a lower moment bound whose exponential base eventually dominates the maximal unbalanced support bound.

Theorem 5.1 compares every Gr_C(3,6) two-level multiplicity coefficientwise. The discrete inequalities in Equations (5.10)-(5.13) correctly convert polynomial/exponential terms into monotone normalized sequences with positive base cases.

Theorem 8.1 combines exact rational Hankel coefficients through m=134 with a strict tail ratio already above one at m=134; the overlap of finite and analytic ranges closes every even Taylor coefficient without floating-point sign decisions.

Theorem 7.1 uses the correct zero budget: equal moments through order two give a triple zero at the origin, four density sign changes permit only one further real zero, and the larger positive support endpoint forces that zero to exist and be simple.

Fresh execution of run_all_replays.py passed all five theorem-bearing checks, including 220 Schur-Weyl fixtures, the r=4 exact coefficient range, and exact Q(sqrt(6)) Sturm counts; exact_moment_screen.py found no counterexample in 351 additional cases.
weaknesses: Corollary 6.1 imports the Jacobi-Stein constrained-Hessian operator, its sign convention, and balanced Morse-Bott stability from ARR-2026-6F8XRSBM0J9Q2R2B. The public primary PDF corroborates those formulas and theorems, but the dependency is not self-contained here.

Lemma 7.2 cites the extended-complete-Chebyshev interpolation theorem behind multiplicity-counting variation diminution. The proof sketch is credible, but a theorem number and hypotheses covering piecewise-polynomial signed densities would make the crossing certificate easier to audit.

The full-spectrum global maximizer remains open. Consequently the branch order cannot by itself select the true matrix-Bingham envelope; the manuscript states this boundary correctly, but it substantially limits operational consequences.
